characterList.description: A middle-aged man with short black hair and a mustache, wearing black rectangular glasses and a light blue and white checkered shirt. He is the Chairperson of Religious Liberty Forum, Nepal.
characterList.name: Pr. Tanka Subedi

content_metadata.description: A video featuring Pr. Tanka Subedi, chairperson of the Religious Liberty Forum in Nepal, addressing the rising religious tensions and challenges faced by the Christian community in Nepal.

qAndA.answer: The EU report on the recent elections in Nepal.
qAndA.question: What is the source of the information that the Prime Minister used to make his statement against Christians?
What is the name of the organization that published the false press release blaming Christians for planning to destroy temples and build churches?

qAndA.answer: The shooting of a Hindu priest in Biratnagar.
qAndA.question: What specific incident is used as evidence to accuse Christians even though they had no involvement?

qAndA.answer: To refute claims that Christians are a foreign influence or a threat to Nepali culture. He aims to counter the narrative that Christians are working with external forces to undermine Hinduism.
qAndA.question: Why does Pr. Subedi emphasize the indigenous nature of the Christian community in Nepal?

qAndA.answer: He appeals for the government to respect the Christian community, treat them with dignity, and ensure their religious freedom. He seeks recognition and protection for the Christian community as an integral part of Nepalese society.
qAndA.question: What does Pr. Subedi appeal to the government for in the concluding part of the video?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: In the recent time with the new government, we had a very much hope on more freedom and
more systematic policies and things in place.
But unlike many people are thinking the same, but the Prime Minister himself and the
Home Minister, they were not so sensitive about religious issues and they are speaking
publicly on these issues.
So Prime Minister was speaking on EU report on election.
And that report was for election commission in Nepal.
And there is one sentence mentioned by EU, about 1.4 percent Christians in Nepal and why
this is not in the reservation seat.
And on that big document, it is one sentence that is taken by the Prime Minister and making
public statement against Christians and conversion.
And when we heard things from the Prime Minister, that was not what we expect from a
Guardian.
He is our Prime Minister.
So Christians also voted him and many people are following his party and the church.
The second thing is there is a group called Mongol National Army and they have published
a press release sometime ago which looks fake and signed by a person called David Tamang.
We don't know whether that is true or just made up name.
And in the press release, they say that they are going to destroy all the temples and
gumbas and build churches in their places.
And they will declare Nepal a Christian isai rastra, Christian country by 2025.
We have objected on that and said we have no connection with this group.
This is not from the Christian community that was already came out.
But Home Minister took it as a real matter done by Christian and he made public statement
against Christians and said I will be very hard on Christians and conversion and all
that.
And then recently somebody sued Hindu priest in Biratnagar, which were also they left
a leaflet where they say many accusations to Hindus becoming pro-Indian and many other
things.
But it also include destroying Bible.
So because of that one word Bible, some people are taking it as it is done by the Christians.
And there are rallies and things are happening in different cities in Nepal against Christian
speaking against Christian.
And some of the pastors in East Nepal have got threat from unknown people on phone asking
them to bring David Tamang to them.
So we don't know who is David Tamang, whether that person exists and who is Mongol organization
we have no idea.
And the Christian community doesn't have any connection with them.
And also Christian community does not have any formal connection with European Union.
So the Christian community in Nepal is an indigenous religious group.
The government should respect that and look at them with dignity.
So now we are feeling bit and sideline by the government.
That's not what the Christian community in Nepal wants or any other religious group
want.

youtube_description: Professor Tanka Subedi, chairperson of Nepal’s Religious Liberty Forum, tells World Watch Monitor he was shocked at the comments made by the prime minster earlier this year, when he openly criticised foreign Christians for converting people to other religions.
